items.followUp: Using the equations of motion, derive the relation S = ½(Vi + Vf)t.

rubric.why: This gives the first equation of motion needed in the derivation.
rubric.description: Uses the acceleration relation to obtain Vf = Vi + at.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the acceleration definition or its correct rearrangement.

rubric.why: For uniform acceleration, displacement is average velocity multiplied by time.
rubric.description: Relates displacement to average velocity and time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the average-velocity displacement relation.

rubric.why: Substituting Vf = Vi + at into the displacement relation is the key derivation step.
rubric.description: Substitutes the first equation of motion and simplifies correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct substitution or equivalent simplification.
Award 1 mark for the correct final equation.

modelAnswer: For uniform acceleration, average velocity = (Vi + Vf)/2.
From the definition of acceleration: a = (Vf − Vi)/t.
